> Blog · Prestige · 2026-08-01

# Brief
- Title: Clay and Cast Iron: What Older Lowcountry Sewer Lines Are Made Of (and How They Fail)
- Slug: /blog/old-sewer-pipes/. Role: Support 5. Intent: informational and commercial research. About 1,110 words.
- Primary keyword: cast iron sewer pipe. Secondaries: clay sewer pipe, cast iron sewer pipe corrosion, how long do sewer pipes last, signs of an old sewer line, clay vs cast iron sewer pipe.

# Angle
Homes built before the 1980s likely have clay or cast iron laterals; later homes generally use PVC. Clay fails at the joints (ground shift, roots). Cast iron corrodes and scales from the inside. Sections cover materials in older Bluffton and Beaufort neighborhoods, how each fails, lifespan, how to tell what you have (camera), repair vs replace, and an FAQ.

# Flag status
- Links to the trenchless and pillar posts, so publish after the pillar.
- First-hand proof is optional (a local camera still of corroded cast iron or a separated clay joint).
- Gated for Scott: repair, replacement and lining pricing, free language, warranties.

# Status
Drip Day 10 (scheduled 2026-08-11). Not yet published per the cluster list.
